title: How to Secure Your Telegram Account from SIM Swapping and Session Hijacking
excerpt: Because Telegram stores your messages in the cloud, an intercepted SMS code gives hackers your entire chat history. Here is how to lock down your Telegram account with 2FA and relay shields.
description: Essential Telegram security guide: enable Two-Step Verification cloud passwords, terminate rogue active sessions, and prevent IP address leaks on voice calls.
metaTitle: How to Secure Telegram from Hackers and SIM Swapping (2026)
metaDescription: Protect your Telegram account from SIM-swap attacks and unauthorized logins. Enable two-step verification, audit linked devices, and hide your IP address on calls.

faq.title: Why is Telegram more vulnerable to SIM swapping than Signal or WhatsApp?
faq.description: Unlike WhatsApp or Signal where chat histories are stored locally on your device, Telegram's default chats are stored on Telegram's cloud servers. If an attacker intercepts your SMS verification code without 2FA enabled, they immediately download your entire message history, media, and contact list to their machine.

faq.title: What happens if I forget my Telegram Two-Step Verification password?
faq.description: If you forget your 2FA password and did not attach a verified recovery email, you will be permanently locked out of your cloud chat history. Telegram will require you to reset your account, which deletes all past cloud chats, channels you own, and media archives.

faq.title: Does making a Telegram voice call reveal my IP address to the other person?
faq.description: By default, Telegram voice and video calls use Peer-to-Peer (P2P) connections for faster low-latency audio. However, P2P directly connects your device's IP address to the other person's device, exposing your ISP and approximate physical location. You can disable this by setting P2P calls to 'Nobody' or 'My Contacts Only'.

html:
The Fundamental Architectural Risk of Telegram

Telegram is celebrated for its seamless multi-device synchronization: you can type on your iPhone, continue on your Windows laptop, and read on an Android tablet in real time. However, this architectural convenience has a major security prerequisite: by default, Telegram chats are stored in the cloud, not end-to-end encrypted on device storage (only 'Secret Chats' are E2EE).

If a criminal performs a SIM swap on your mobile number or intercepts your telecom SMS token, they can log into Telegram on their desktop and download your entire ten-year chat archive within seconds. Here is how to configure Telegram so that an SMS intercept alone cannot compromise your data.

1. Enable Two-Step Verification (Cloud Password)

The single most important setting on Telegram is the Cloud Password. This ensures that even if someone clones your SIM card or steals your phone number, they cannot log in without entering a secret master password:

  1. Open Telegram and tap Settings > Privacy and Security.
  2. Select Two-Step Verification and tap Set Password.
  3. Choose a strong alphanumeric passphrase (minimum 12 characters).
  4. Provide a password hint that only you understand.
  5. Set a recovery email: Enter a secure email address that is already protected with hardware key or authenticator app 2FA. Confirm the 6-digit verification code sent to your inbox.

2. Audit and Terminate Rogue Active Sessions

Attackers who gain temporary access often leave a background session running on a headless browser or modified desktop client. Audit your active sessions monthly:

  1. Go to Settings > Devices.
  2. Review the list of connected devices. Pay special attention to the operating system, IP location, and date of last access.
  3. If you see any unfamiliar entry (e.g., 'Telegram Web macOS' when you only use Windows), tap on it and select Terminate Session.
  4. Configure 'Automatically terminate old sessions' to 1 month or 3 months so that discarded phones or retired laptops automatically lose access.

3. Block IP Address Leaks on Voice & Video Calls

Many users are unaware that Telegram voice calls establish direct P2P (Peer-to-Peer) network packets to minimize latency. If you receive a call from an unknown user or scammer, packet sniffers (like Wireshark) can capture your real residential IP address.

  1. Open Settings > Privacy and Security > Calls.
  2. Under Peer-to-Peer, change the setting from 'Everybody' to Never (or My Contacts).

When set to 'Never', all voice packets are routed through Telegram's encrypted relay servers. This adds roughly 20 milliseconds of latency, but completely conceals your home IP address from network adversaries.

4. Restrict Phone Number and Forwarding Visibility

Prevent scraping bots from harvesting your phone number across large public Telegram supergroups:

  • Phone Number: Set 'Who can see my phone number' to Nobody, and 'Who can find me by my number' to My Contacts.
  • Forwarded Messages: Set 'Who can add a link to my account when forwarding my messages' to Nobody. This ensures that if someone forwards your message into a spam channel, your username is not clickable.
